attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: A faithful two-part historical observation about how long Tay and the Galactica demo stayed up. Reading 'Galactica' as Meta's hosted public demo fits the context.

contract.note: Reading 'lasted three days' as roughly three days of elapsed time is the ordinary plain reading. Counting calendar dates inclusively would be a looser reading the speaker did not give. The result for Galactica depends on which reading is used.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, reporting at the time, says Tay was silenced after 16 hours of chats, and Microsoft confirmed it was taken offline.
MIT Technology Review uses the phrase 'three days', but its own dates (launch Nov 15, demo pulled Nov 17) mean about two elapsed days. So it does not establish three elapsed days.
CNET, reporting at the time, says the demo was paused within 48 hours of release. That falls short of roughly three elapsed days.

reviews.rationale: The Tay part holds: TechCrunch reports 16 hours, and Microsoft confirmed it took Tay offline. The Galactica part does not hold on the elapsed-time reading. CNET says the demo was paused within 48 hours, and MIT Technology Review's dates (Nov 15 to Nov 17) also point to about two days, despite its 'three days' wording. The contract's contradiction condition is met for Galactica only.
